algorithm: Convert preservation of the mean into a pair-sum equation and count complements among previously seen values.
correctness_argument: The equality (S-a_i-a_j)/(n-2)=S/n is equivalent to a_i+a_j=2S/n. If the right side is nonintegral no pair works. Adding counts of prior complements counts each unordered pair exactly once.
problem_understanding: Let S denote the original sum.

steps.claim: Let S denote the original sum.
steps.rationale: Let S denote the original sum.

steps.claim: The removed pair sum must equal one copy of the original mean.
steps.rationale: The removed pair sum must equal one copy of the original mean.

steps.claim: The equality (S-a_i-a_j)/(n-2)=S/n is equivalent to a_i+a_j=2S/n. If the right side is nonintegral no pair works. Adding counts of prior complements counts each unordered pair exactly once.
steps.rationale: The equality (S-a_i-a_j)/(n-2)=S/n is equivalent to a_i+a_j=2S/n. If the right side is nonintegral no pair works. Adding counts of prior complements counts each unordered pair exactly once.

steps.claim: Time: O(n log n); space: O(n).
steps.rationale: Time: O(n log n); space: O(n).

steps.claim: Implementation follows these obligations: Let S denote the original sum. Equal means require the removed pair sum to equal 2S/n. Reject a nonintegral target using exact arithmetic. Count complements among earlier positions only. Accumulate the number of pairs in 64 bits.
steps.rationale: Implementation follows these obligations: Let S denote the original sum. Equal means require the removed pair sum to equal 2S/n. Reject a nonintegral target using exact arithmetic. Count complements among earlier positions only. Accumulate the number of pairs in 64 bits.
